name: pH Determination
teachingNotes: pH measurement quantifies the hydrogen ion activity (-log10[H+]). Test papers offer quick semi-quantitative estimates (±1 pH unit), while calibrated glass electrodes measure potentiometrically with high precision (±0.02 pH units).

steps.prompt: Step 1: Choose measurement method. Select between 'pH Indicator Paper', 'Indicator Solution', or 'Calibrated pH Meter'.
steps.hint: Click one of the method tabs on the workbench action bar to choose your analytical technique.
steps.completionText: Method selected. In this lab, we will demonstrate indicator paper estimation and calibrated electrometric meter measurement.

steps.prompt: Step 2: Indicator Paper: Touch a drop of sample liquid onto the paper strip using a clean glass rod or dropper.
steps.hint: Do NOT dunk the whole strip into the reagent stock! Touch a single drop onto the test paper using the glass stirring rod.
steps.completionText: Sample droplet transferred to indicator paper strip. Chemical dyes react and develop color.

steps.prompt: Step 3: Compare against standard chart. Drag or select the matching color band to estimate pH.
steps.hint: Compare the developed strip color against the standard reference chart under good lighting. Note: this provides an estimate only!
steps.completionText: Color matched! Illustrative estimated pH: ~3.0 (Acidic). Indicator paper provides a fast screening estimate.

steps.prompt: Step 4: pH Meter: Rinse the combination electrode with wash bottle, then immerse in standard pH 7.0 buffer.
steps.hint: Click 'Rinse & Calibrate' to rinse the electrode with distilled water and calibrate against standard buffer solution.
steps.completionText: Electrode rinsed and calibrated against standard buffer (offset and slope calibrated per manufacturer protocol).

steps.prompt: Step 5: Rinse electrode with wash bottle and immerse in illustrative Sample A to take digital reading.
steps.hint: Always rinse the electrode with distilled water between buffer and sample to prevent cross-contamination.
steps.completionText: Illustrative digital pH reading stabilized: 2.85 ± 0.02. Technique verified!

dunk_stock.message: Contamination mistake: Never immerse test paper strips directly into the main sample bottle. Transfer a droplet using a clean glass rod or spot plate.

skip_calibration.message: Analytical error: Attempting to measure sample pH without first calibrating the meter against standard buffers yields uncalibrated, inaccurate readings.

no_rinse.message: Cross-contamination: Forgetting to rinse the electrode with distilled water carries over buffer salts into the sample, skewing the pH measurement.
